name: Ninnisig
description: A star 255 parsecs away, 65 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: radius 65.259 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1578.8 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: effective temperature 4507 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.07)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.6 from 1995AJ....110.2425L, the median of its 3 spectra; the 8 published values span log g 1.6 to 1.93, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: distance 255.102 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.043), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 255 parsecs away, 65 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,579 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,507 K, so 65.259 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 94713: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Theta Lyrae
quotes.card: Theta Lyrae, also named Ninnisig, is a red giant star in the constellation Lyra, approximately 760 light-years away from Earth.
